root_decision: Adopt the finite protocol. Scientific execution requires a separate source/input/review-bound release after implementation qualification.
adoption_reason: Ten saved states isolate distinct numerical failure mechanisms and matched controls without shared-parameter fitting or new initialization. Reusing cached main/fine trajectories avoids redundant scientific work; cross-method accepted trajectories distinguish finite-interval growth from attempted-stage failures.
execution_clarifications: Use public SciPy solver interfaces. Internal rejection counts not exposed by those interfaces are null. Count outer step attempts separately; terminal-attempt callbacks are attempted states, not automatically all rejected states. Preserve accepted meshes independently and count every actual RHS callback including finite-difference Jacobians and dense interpolation.
Four-grid error ratios share min(t_star, last valid 0.01 s sample of all four paths). No upward rounding, interpolation across failed output, or replacement of an unqualified reference.
Observation-level convergence and full-state convergence are reported separately. Growth labels require the three-reference full-state and observation agreement specified by the protocol.

Do not modify original source, initializers, model parameters, stage selection, deployment steps or old evidence. The optional zero-term version is separately frozen and requires the stated trigger and algebraic equivalence checks.
